name: Future Perfect and Future Continuous
pt: Future continuous (will be + -ing) mostra uma ação em andamento num momento futuro: 'Amanhã a esta hora estarei voando'. Future perfect (will have + particípio) mostra uma ação que já estará concluída até um momento futuro: 'Até sexta terei terminado'. Armadilha comum: usar o futuro simples (will finish) para tudo, ou traduzir 'terei feito' como 'I will have make'. O verbo depois de will have é sempre o particípio passado.
en: Use the future continuous for an action in progress at a specific future time. Use the future perfect for an action that will be completed before a specific future time (often with by or by the time).
form: will be + verb-ing / will have + past participle
ex: This time tomorrow, I will be flying to London.
By Friday, we will have finished the report.
She will have left by the time you arrive.
cmp: Future simple is a decision or prediction (I will call you). Future continuous is in progress at a time (I will be working at 8). Future perfect is finished before a time (I will have finished by 8).

mistakes.bad: By next year, I will finish my course.
mistakes.good: By next year, I will have finished my course.
mistakes.why: With 'by' + a future time, use the future perfect for a completed action.

mistakes.bad: She will have finish the work by noon.
mistakes.good: She will have finished the work by noon.
mistakes.why: After will have, use the past participle.

mistakes.bad: At 9 tomorrow I will work in the office.
mistakes.good: At 9 tomorrow I will be working in the office.
mistakes.why: An action in progress at a future moment needs the future continuous.

exercises.q: By next June, I ____ in this company for ten years.
exercises.why: Completed duration up to a future point: will have + past participle.

exercises.q: This time tomorrow, we ____ on a plane to Lisbon.
exercises.why: Action in progress at a future time: will be + -ing.

exercises.q: Don't call at 8. I ____ dinner.
exercises.why: In progress at 8: will be having.

exercises.q: Choose the correct sentence:
opts: She will has finished by five.
She will have finished by five.
She will have finish by five.

exercises.q: By the time you arrive, the meeting ____.
exercises.why: The meeting will be completed (started) before your arrival: future perfect.

exercises.q: In ten years, scientists ____ a cure for many diseases.
exercises.why: Completed before a future time: will have found.

exercises.q: By 2030, she ____ (graduate) from university.
exercises.why: Future perfect: will have + past participle.

exercises.q: This time next week, I ____ (lie) on a beach.
By the end of the month, we ____ (not/finish) the project.
exercises.why: Negative future perfect: won't have + past participle.

exercises.q: This time tomorrow, he ____ (drive) to Rio.
Até sexta, terei terminado o relatório.
exercises.ans: I will have finished the report by Friday.

exercises.q: Amanhã a esta hora, estarei voando para Londres.
exercises.ans: This time tomorrow, I will be flying to London.
exercises.why: Future continuous for an action in progress.

exercises.q: Eles já terão saído quando você chegar.
exercises.ans: They will have left by the time you arrive.
exercises.why: Future perfect + present simple after by the time.

exercises.q: Ela estará trabalhando às oito.
exercises.ans: She will be working at eight.

name: Causative: Have / Get Something Done
pt: Usamos have/get + objeto + particípio passado quando outra pessoa faz o serviço para nós (ou quando algo nos acontece). 'Cortei o cabelo' no salão = 'I had my hair cut', não 'I cut my hair' (que significa que você mesmo cortou). Armadilha comum: dizer 'I cut my hair' ou 'I have cut my hair' por causa do português, que usa o mesmo verbo nos dois casos. 'Get' é mais informal. O verbo principal é que muda de tempo: had, am having, will have.
en: We use have or get + object + past participle when someone else does a service for us, or when something happens to us (often something unpleasant).
ex: I had my car repaired yesterday.
We are having the kitchen painted.
He got his wallet stolen on the train.
cmp: 'I repaired my car' means I did it myself. 'I had my car repaired' means someone else did it.

mistakes.bad: I cut my hair yesterday at the salon.
mistakes.good: I had my hair cut yesterday at the salon.
mistakes.why: A professional did it, so use the causative.

mistakes.bad: She had her house to paint.
mistakes.good: She had her house painted.
mistakes.why: Use the past participle, not an infinitive.

mistakes.bad: I will have repaired my phone tomorrow by a technician.
mistakes.good: I will have my phone repaired tomorrow.
mistakes.why: This is the causative, not the future perfect.

exercises.q: I ____ my car repaired yesterday.
exercises.why: Past causative: had + object + past participle.

exercises.q: She is going to ____ her hair cut tomorrow.
exercises.why: After going to, use the base form have.

exercises.q: Which sentence is correct?
opts: We had the kitchen painted last week.
We had the kitchen paint last week.
We had painted the kitchen by a decorator last week.
We had the kitchen to paint last week.

exercises.q: I need to ____ my passport renewed.
exercises.why: After need to, use the base form get.

exercises.q: He had his wallet ____ on the train.
exercises.why: Something happened to him: had + object + past participle.

exercises.q: Which sentence means a professional did the work?
exercises.why: get + object + past participle means someone else did it.

exercises.q: She ____ (have) her nails done yesterday.
He ____ (get) his hair cut last Friday.
They are having their house ____ (paint) at the moment.
I ____ (not/have) my car washed last week.
exercises.why: Negative past: didn't + base verb have.

exercises.q: Eu cortei o cabelo ontem (no salão).
exercises.ans: I had my hair cut yesterday.
exercises.why: Causative for a service done by someone else.

exercises.q: Precisamos consertar o telhado (alguém vai fazer).
exercises.ans: We need to get the roof repaired.
exercises.why: need to get + object + past participle.

exercises.q: Ele mandou lavar o carro.
Vou mandar consertar meu computador amanhã.
exercises.ans: I am going to have my computer fixed tomorrow.
exercises.why: going to + have + object + past participle.

name: Quantifiers
pt: Quantifiers dizem 'quanto' ou 'quantos'. Com substantivos contáveis: many, few, a few, several. Com incontáveis: much, little, a little. Com ambos: a lot of, plenty of, enough, some. Few e little têm sentido negativo ('quase nenhum'); a few e a little têm sentido positivo ('alguns/um pouco'). Armadilha comum: dizer 'many money' ou 'much people' (em português 'muito' serve para os dois), e confundir 'little' com 'a little'. Enough vem antes do substantivo (enough time) e depois do adjetivo (old enough).
en: Use many/few/a few with countable nouns and much/little/a little with uncountable nouns. Few and little mean not enough; a few and a little mean some. Plenty of and enough work with both.
form: many/few/a few + plural noun; much/little/a little + uncountable noun
ex: How much money do you have?
Few people came to the meeting.
There is plenty of room in the car.
cmp: 'I have a little time' means some time, enough to help. 'I have little time' means almost none.

mistakes.bad: How many money do you have?
mistakes.good: How much money do you have?
mistakes.why: Money is uncountable, so use much.

mistakes.bad: I have too much friends.
mistakes.good: I have too many friends.
mistakes.why: Friends is countable, so use many.

mistakes.bad: I don't have time enough.
mistakes.good: I don't have enough time.
mistakes.why: Enough comes before a noun.

exercises.q: How ____ money do you have?
There are only ____ seats left, so hurry.
exercises.why: Seats are countable and the idea is negative: few.

exercises.q: Can I have ____ sugar in my coffee?
exercises.why: Sugar is uncountable and the idea is positive: a little.

exercises.q: Which sentence is correct?
'I have little patience' means:
exercises.why: Little without 'a' has a negative meaning.

exercises.q: There is ____ of room in the car, so bring your bags.
exercises.why: Plenty of works with uncountable nouns like room.

exercises.q: How ____ people came to the party?
She has very ____ time left, so she can't help us.
Are you old ____ to drive?
I know ____ good restaurants nearby (some, enough to choose from).
Quanto dinheiro você tem?
exercises.ans: How much money do you have?

exercises.q: Poucas pessoas vieram à reunião.
exercises.ans: Few people came to the meeting.

exercises.q: Há bastante espaço no carro.
exercises.ans: There is plenty of room in the car.

exercises.q: Não tenho tempo suficiente.

name: Question Tags and Indirect Questions
pt: Question tags são perguntinhas no fim da frase ('..., não é?'). Frase afirmativa leva tag negativa e vice-versa, repetindo o auxiliar: 'You live here, don't you?'. Casos especiais: 'I am' vira 'aren't I?' e 'Let's' vira 'shall we?'. Já nas perguntas indiretas ('Could you tell me...?'), a ordem volta a ser de afirmação, sem do/does/did: 'Do you know where the bank is?'. Armadilha comum: dizer 'where is the bank' dentro da pergunta indireta e usar 'isn't it?' para tudo, como o 'né?' do português. Para sim/não use if ou whether.
en: A question tag is a short question added to a statement. Use a negative tag after a positive statement and a positive tag after a negative one. In indirect questions, use statement word order with no inversion and no do/does/did.
form: positive statement, negative tag? / negative statement, positive tag? / Could you tell me + wh-word + subject + verb
ex: You live here, don't you?
She hasn't called, has she?
Could you tell me what time it is?
cmp: Direct: Where is the bank? Indirect: Do you know where the bank is? (the verb moves after the subject).

mistakes.bad: You live here, isn't it?
mistakes.good: You live here, don't you?
mistakes.why: The tag repeats the auxiliary and matches the subject.

mistakes.bad: Could you tell me where is the bank?
mistakes.good: Could you tell me where the bank is?
mistakes.why: Indirect questions use statement word order.

mistakes.bad: Do you know what time does the train leave?
mistakes.good: Do you know what time the train leaves?
mistakes.why: Do not use does in an indirect question.

exercises.q: You live in Recife, ____?
exercises.why: Positive statement in present simple: don't you.

exercises.q: She hasn't called, ____?
exercises.why: Negative statement with has: positive tag has she.

exercises.q: I'm late, ____?
exercises.why: The tag for I am is aren't I.

exercises.q: Which indirect question is correct?
opts: Could you tell me where is the bank?
Could you tell me where the bank is?
Could you tell me where does the bank is?

exercises.q: Do you know ____ the store opens at nine?
exercises.why: Yes/no indirect questions use if or whether.

exercises.q: Let's go home, ____?
exercises.why: The tag for Let's is shall we.

exercises.q: They can swim, ____ they?
exercises.why: Positive statement, negative tag with the same modal.

exercises.q: He doesn't smoke, ____ he?
Could you tell me what time the train ____ (leave)?
exercises.why: Statement word order: the train leaves.

exercises.q: I wonder ____ she is married.
exercises.why: Use if or whether in a yes/no indirect question.

exercises.q: Você mora aqui, não é?
Você sabe onde fica o banco?
exercises.ans: Do you know where the bank is?
exercises.why: Indirect question with statement word order.

exercises.q: Você poderia me dizer que horas são?
exercises.ans: Could you tell me what time it is?
exercises.why: Indirect question: what time it is.

exercises.q: Ela não está em casa, está?
exercises.ans: She isn't at home, is she?

name: Cleft Sentences: Advanced Focus
pt: Frases clivadas colocam foco em uma parte da frase. It-cleft: 'It was the manager who approved the budget' (foco em quem) ou 'It was in Paris that I met Ana' (foco em onde). Wh-cleft: 'What I need is a long holiday'. Existem ainda 'All I want is...', 'What happened was that...' e a versão invertida 'A long holiday is what I need'. Armadilha comum: traduzir 'Foi ele que...' com 'was him that' ou esquecer o that/who, e usar 'All what I want'. Depois de what-cleft com verbo de ação, o verbo seguinte fica no infinitivo: 'What she did was resign'.
en: Cleft sentences split one idea into two clauses to put focus on one part. Use it + be + focus + that/who, or a wh-clause + be + focus. Use 'All (that) I...' for 'only'.
form: It + be + focus + that/who... / What + subject + verb + be + focus
ex: It was in Paris that I met Ana.
What I need is a good rest.
What happened was that the power went out.
cmp: It-clefts focus on who, where or when. Wh-clefts focus on the thing, the action or the result.

mistakes.bad: All what I want is peace.
mistakes.good: All I want is peace.
mistakes.why: Do not add what after all.

mistakes.bad: What she did was resigned without notice.
mistakes.good: What she did was resign without notice.
mistakes.why: After 'What ... did was', use the base form or to-infinitive.

mistakes.bad: What I need are a long holiday.
mistakes.good: What I need is a long holiday.
mistakes.why: A what-clause takes a singular verb with a singular focus.

exercises.q: It was the manager ____ approved the budget.
exercises.why: A person as subject in an it-cleft: who.

exercises.q: What I need ____ a long holiday.
exercises.why: What-cleft with a singular focus: is.

exercises.q: What she did ____ to resign without notice.
Which sentence emphasises WHERE they met?
opts: It was Ana that I met in Paris.
It was in Paris that I met Ana.
What I met was Ana in Paris.
exercises.why: The focus phrase comes right after It was.

exercises.q: Which sentence is correct?
opts: All I want is a quiet evening.
All what I want is a quiet evening.
All I want are a quiet evening.
exercises.why: All + clause + is, with no what.

exercises.q: What happened ____ that the power went out.
It was my sister ____ told me the news.
exercises.why: A person as subject: who or that.

exercises.q: ____ I really enjoyed was the soundtrack.
What we should do ____ talk to the client directly.
It was not until midnight ____ the guests left.
exercises.why: It was not until + time + that.

exercises.q: Foi o gerente quem aprovou o orçamento.
exercises.ans: It was the manager who approved the budget.

exercises.q: O que eu preciso é de um bom descanso.
exercises.ans: What I need is a good rest.

exercises.q: Foi em 2019 que nos conhecemos.
exercises.ans: It was in 2019 that we met.

exercises.q: Tudo o que eu quero é paz e sossego.
exercises.ans: All I want is peace and quiet.

name: Subjunctive and Formal Structures
pt: Em inglês formal, depois de verbos como suggest, recommend, insist, demand, propose e de adjetivos como essential, vital, important, usamos that + sujeito + verbo na forma base, sem -s e sem to: 'I suggest that he go', 'It is vital that she be here'. A negação é 'not + verbo base'. Armadilha comum: usar infinitivo como no português ('Ele sugeriu mim to go'; 'exigiu ele to pay') ou conjugar o verbo ('that he pays'). Também: 'as if he were' (were para todas as pessoas) e 'Be that as it may' (seja como for).
en: After verbs of suggestion, demand or recommendation, and after adjectives like essential or vital, formal English uses that + subject + base verb. The verb does not change for person or tense.
form: suggest/insist/demand/recommend + that + subject + base verb; It is vital that + subject + base verb
ex: The doctor recommended that he get more rest.
It is essential that every employee submit the form.
She talks as if she were the boss.
cmp: Normal: He suggests that Tom goes. Formal subjunctive: He suggests that Tom go. Both are used, but the second is formal.

mistakes.bad: She suggested me to take a taxi.
mistakes.good: She suggested that I take a taxi.
mistakes.why: Suggest is not followed by object + to-infinitive.

mistakes.bad: I demand that he is here at once.
mistakes.good: I demand that he be here at once.
mistakes.why: The subjunctive uses the base form be.

mistakes.bad: It is vital that nobody doesn't be late.
mistakes.good: It is vital that nobody be late.
mistakes.why: No do-support in the subjunctive, and no double negative.

exercises.q: The doctor recommended that he ____ more rest.
It is essential that every employee ____ the form by Friday.
In formal English: It is vital that nobody ____ late.
exercises.why: Subjunctive uses the base form be.

exercises.q: Which sentence is correct?
opts: She suggested that I take a taxi.
She suggested me to take a taxi.
She suggested me taking a taxi.

exercises.q: He talks as if he ____ the boss.
'Be that as it may' means:
exercises.why: It accepts a point but moves on to another.

exercises.q: The judge ordered that the defendant ____ (pay) a fine.
I demand that he ____ (be) here at once.
It is important that she ____ (not/forget) her passport.
The committee proposed that the meeting ____ (postpone) until May.
Ele insistiu que ela pagasse a conta.
exercises.ans: He insisted that she pay the bill.

exercises.q: É essencial que todos cheguem a tempo.
exercises.ans: It is essential that everyone arrive on time.

exercises.q: Ela sugeriu que eu tomasse um táxi.
exercises.ans: She suggested that I take a taxi.

exercises.q: Ele fala como se fosse o dono.
exercises.ans: He talks as if he were the owner.

name: Advanced Articles and Determiners
pt: Sem artigo: generalizações com substantivos incontáveis ou plurais ('Life is difficult', 'Dogs are loyal'). Com 'the': coisas únicas, superlativos, ordinais, 'the + adjetivo' para grupos (the rich, the poor), países no plural ou com Republic/Kingdom (the Netherlands, the United States), instrumentos musicais (play the piano). Instituições usadas pela função não levam artigo (in hospital, at school – inglês britânico). Armadilha comum: dizer 'The life is difficult' ou 'I love the music', copiando 'A vida é difícil'. Determinantes: each/every/both/either/neither, 'the whole day' (não 'whole the day'), 'What a beautiful view!'.
en: Use no article for general ideas with plural or uncountable nouns. Use the for unique things, superlatives, groups like the rich, and some place names. Choose the right determiner: each, every, both, either, neither, the whole.
form: the + superlative / the + adjective / the whole + singular noun / What a(n) + adjective + noun
ex: Life is difficult sometimes.
She spent the whole day studying.
What a beautiful view!
cmp: 'I love music' is music in general. 'I love the music in this film' is a specific one.

mistakes.bad: The life is full of surprises.
mistakes.good: Life is full of surprises.
mistakes.why: No article for a general abstract noun.

mistakes.bad: She spent whole the day reading.
mistakes.good: She spent the whole day reading.
mistakes.why: The whole: the comes first.

mistakes.bad: What beautiful view!
mistakes.good: What a beautiful view!
mistakes.why: What + a + adjective + singular countable noun.

exercises.q: ____ life is full of surprises.
exercises.why: No article for a general abstract noun.

exercises.q: Of all the cities I visited, Lisbon was ____ best.
In British English, 'My brother is in hospital' means:
opts: He works there as a doctor.
exercises.why: No article: the institution is used for its purpose.

exercises.q: What ____ beautiful view!
____ of my two brothers lives in Canada.
exercises.why: Each of + plural noun takes a singular verb.

exercises.q: She spent ____ day reading.
I'd like ____ umbrella, please.
We visited ____ Netherlands last summer.
exercises.why: The Netherlands is a plural name.

exercises.q: She plays ____ piano very well.
The rich ____ not always happy.
A vida é difícil às vezes.
exercises.why: No article for a general abstract noun.

exercises.q: Que vista linda!
Ela passou o dia inteiro estudando.
exercises.ans: She spent the whole day studying.

exercises.q: Eles moram nos Estados Unidos.
exercises.ans: They live in the United States.

name: Emphasis and Contrast Structures
pt: Para dar ênfase, use do/does/did antes do verbo base em frases afirmativas: 'I do like your plan' (eu realmente gosto). Para contraste: although/even though + oração ('Although he was tired, he kept working'); despite/in spite of + substantivo ou -ing ('Despite the rain...'); whereas/while para comparar dois fatos; however em outra frase, entre vírgulas ou depois de ponto e vírgula. Armadilhas comuns: 'Although..., but...' (em inglês, só um conectivo), 'despite of' (o certo é despite ou in spite of) e 'Despite he was tired'.
en: Use do/does/did + base verb to emphasise a positive statement. Contrast with although + clause, despite + noun/-ing, whereas for two opposite facts, and however to start a new idea.
form: do/does/did + base verb / although + clause / despite + noun or -ing / ..., whereas ... / ; however,
ex: I do like your plan, but it is too expensive.
Although he was tired, he kept working.
Despite the rain, we went out.
cmp: Although is followed by a clause. Despite is followed by a noun or -ing. However is a linking adverb, not a conjunction.

mistakes.bad: Although he was tired, but he kept working.
mistakes.good: Although he was tired, he kept working.
mistakes.why: Do not use although and but together.

mistakes.bad: Despite of the rain, we went out.
mistakes.good: Despite the rain, we went out.
mistakes.why: Despite is never followed by of; in spite of is the longer form.

mistakes.bad: Despite it was raining, we went out.
mistakes.good: Although it was raining, we went out.
mistakes.why: Despite cannot be followed by a full clause.

exercises.q: I ____ like your plan, but it is too expensive.
She ____ call you yesterday; maybe she used the wrong number.
____ it was raining, we went for a walk.
____ the rain, we went out.
exercises.why: Despite is followed by a noun.

exercises.q: Which sentence is correct?
opts: Although he was tired, he kept working.
Although he was tired, but he kept working.
Despite of being tired, he kept working.
exercises.why: Use only one contrast connector and no 'of' after despite.

exercises.q: My sister loves coffee, ____ I prefer tea.
He ____ say sorry, but nobody believed him.
____ the traffic, we arrived on time.
exercises.why: Despite or in spite of before a noun.

exercises.q: I like cats; ____, my brother prefers dogs.
exercises.why: However links two sentences, after a semicolon.

exercises.q: ____ she studied hard, she failed the exam.
exercises.why: Although introduces a clause of contrast.

exercises.q: Embora estivesse cansado, ele continuou trabalhando.
exercises.ans: Although he was tired, he kept working.

exercises.q: Apesar da chuva, nós saímos.
exercises.ans: Despite the rain, we went out.

exercises.q: Eu realmente gosto do seu plano.
Ela é rica; no entanto, não é feliz.
exercises.ans: She is rich; however, she is not happy.
exercises.why: however after a semicolon, followed by a comma.
